inspirations.name: ELIZA / Joseph Weizenbaum
inspirations.license: Historical and visual inspiration; no ELIZA code or assets included
inspirations.note: Joseph Weizenbaum’s 1966 ELIZA paper is the starting point for this conversational terminal homage. The monospace interface and quiet blue, gray, and black palette are an original interpretation.

inspirations.name: ENIAC
inspirations.license: Historical inspiration; no historical code, photographs or assets included
inspirations.note: Penn’s account of ENIAC’s 1946 launch honors the people and work behind early electronic computing. The design lesson drawn here is to make controls and results clear.

inspirations.name: IBM AS/400
inspirations.license: Historical inspiration; no IBM code, trademarks as branding, or assets included
inspirations.note: IBM introduced the AS/400 in 1988, emphasizing ease of use, connectivity, and compatibility. AS/400 is the tentative match for Taylor’s remembered AS series.

inspirations.name: InfoDog and MB-F
inspirations.license: Referenced website; its content and trademarks retain their own rights
inspirations.note: A tribute to direct links, useful records, show information, and a community served over time. MB-F traces its dog-show business to 1900; InfoDog displays a 1996–2026 copyright range. The early computer vendor behind InfoDog remains unverified.

inspirations.name: Jack Onofrio Dog Shows
inspirations.license: Referenced website; no website code, images, or logos included
inspirations.note: A tribute to clear routes for entries, upcoming shows, results, and downloads. In a 2015 WEB400 post, Onofrio developer Joe W. Holt described an IBM i server using Apache and RPG/CGIDEV2. That first-person account records the system in use at the time.

inspirations.name: Sashiko
inspirations.note: Roman Gushchin and colleagues developed Sashiko; its announcement credits Chris Mason’s separate review-prompts foundation. Its separation of threads, review stages, status and findings informed this site. No Sashiko source, prompts, kernel patches, branding assets or other website assets were copied into this app.

inspirations.name: DEGS v2.1 Python translation
inspirations.license: MIT for original DEGS; Apache-2.0 for identified Sashiko-derived portions
inspirations.note: Taylor’s selected Python translation was read for its stage provenance and separate concern/result collections. No translated code or prompts were imported into this app. The upstream notices identify the exact authorship, modifications and license boundaries.
